hypotheses.justification: The proof uses `hc` only in the case `c < 0`. The statement also holds when `0 ≤ c`, so a proof can begin with `by_cases hc : c < 0`. If `c < 0`, the existing proof works unchanged. Otherwise `0 ≤ c`, and then `strictTail c b = 0`. To see this, recall that `strictTail c b` is defined as `⟨truncGT c ↑b, _⟩`. By `HahnSeries.coeff_truncGT`, its coefficient at `g` is `if c < g then b.coeff g else 0`. When `c < g`, we have `g > c ≥ 0`, so `g ∉ Iic 0`. Since `b.property` says that the support of `b` lies in `Iic 0`, `b.coeff g = 0`. So every coefficient vanishes, and `Subtype.ext` together with `HahnSeries.ext` gives `strictTail c b = 0`. Then `hasLowerTruncationDegree_zero m` (in LowerTruncationDegree.lean, stated under the same variables) proves `HasLowerTruncationDegree 0 m`, which is the conclusion. In this branch the hypothesis `h` is not even needed. The other binders cannot be removed: `h` is essential for `c < 0`, `b`, `m` and `c` appear in the conclusion, and all the section instances are needed to elaborate `ν = cantorBendixsonDegreeValuation`, whose underlying valuation uses multiplicativity under the full set of hypotheses.
